title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, carried over from the previous pages. X is a (complex-analytic) curve with a ramification datum d_X : X^! -> N supported on a discrete set X^!. A group 𝒢 acts on X compatibly with d_X. G ⊂ 𝒢 is a normal subgroup, Y = X/G, ℋ = 𝒢/G, and d_Y(b) = d_X(a)·|G_a| for b = f(a). The previous page shows that the functor Rev(X,d_X,𝒢) -> Rev(Y,d_Y,ℋ) is an equivalence of categories. In modern terms this is the statement that the quotient orbifold stack [(X,d_X)/G] is equivalent to the orbifold (Y,d_Y), equivariantly for ℋ.

Corollary. For a point x outside X^! with image y outside Y^!, one gets a canonical isomorphism π_1((X,d_X,𝒢),x) ≅ π_1((Y,d_Y,ℋ),y). This is the isomorphism of fundamental groups of the equivalent quotient stacks [(X,d_X)/𝒢] ≃ [(Y,d_Y)/ℋ].

Explicit description in terms of paths.
- An element α of π_1((X,d_X,𝒢),x) is given by a pair (γ,l): γ ∈ 𝒢, and l is the class of a path in U = X∖X^! from x to γ^{-1}x.
- Two pairs (γ,l) and (γ',l') give the same element iff γ = γ' and the loop l'^{-1}l lies in the kernel of π_1(U,x) -> π_1((X,d_X),x).
- That kernel is the normal subgroup generated by the λ_a^{d_X(a)}, a ∈ X^!, where λ_a is the class of a small loop at x around a.
- This is the standard presentation of the orbifold fundamental group of a quotient: an extension of 𝒢 by π_1^orb(X,d_X).

The map, finished on the next page: (γ,l) ↦ (γ̇, f_U(l)), where γ̇ is the image of γ in ℋ and f_U : U -> V = Y∖Y^! ≅ U/G. It is well defined because π_1(f_U) sends λ_a to λ_b^{ν(a)}, with ν(a) = |G_a|. Hence λ_a^{d_X(a)} goes to λ_b^{d_Y(b)}.

The page serves the 'équation des lacets' project. The next page applies it to X = P^1∖{0,1,∞}, with 𝒢 = 𝔖_3 × Z/2 (complex conjugation) and G = 𝔖_3, using the quotient map f(z) = (27/4) z^2(z-1)^2/(z^2-z+1)^3, a normalized inverse of the j-invariant (λ-line -> j-line). The aim is to compute orbifold and Teichmüller-type fundamental groups of M_{0,4}/𝔖_3 and of M_{1,1}, with explicit paths.
errors: The equivalence condition is written 'l'^{-1}l'. Whether this is a loop at x depends on the path-composition convention: l goes from x to γ^{-1}x and l' has the same endpoints. Under either convention the resulting loop is based at x or at γ^{-1}x, so the condition is consistent up to that convention. No real error.
The statement implicitly assumes G is normal in 𝒢 and that the defining relation d_Y(b) = d_X(a)|G_a| holds. Both are taken from earlier pages.

ideas.what: Description of the fundamental group of an orbifold quotient [(X,d_X)/𝒢] by pairs (group element, path from x to γ^{-1}x) modulo the relations λ_a^{d_X(a)}
ideas.modern_name: orbifold / equivariant fundamental group of a quotient stack (extension 1 -> π_1^orb(X) -> π_1^orb([X/𝒢]) -> 𝒢 -> 1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thurston (orbifolds, 1978-80), Haefliger, Bass (path-group description); classical for discontinuous groups (Armstrong, 1960s)
ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in SGA1 (tame fundamental group with ramification) and La Longue Marche; unsure about the explicit path formulation.

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism π_1((X,d_X,𝒢),x) ≅ π_1((X/G,d_Y,𝒢/G),y), with ramification indices multiplied by stabilizer orders
ideas.modern_name: invariance of the orbifold fundamental group under passing to the quotient by a normal subgroup ([X/G]/ℋ ≃ [X/𝒢])

ideas.what: Local computation: a loop λ_a maps to λ_b^{ν(a)}, with ν(a) the ramification index, giving d_Y = d_X·ν
ideas.modern_name: local monodromy under a ramified cover

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard explicit description of orbifold fundamental groups of quotients. It is a preparatory step for the λ-line / j-line computation on the following pages; nothing here goes beyond the known literature.
transcription_corrections: 'γ ∈ G' should read 'γ ∈ 𝒢' (script G, the full group), consistent with π_1((X,d_X,𝒢),x).
In formula (21) and the following lines the groups are script 𝒢 and ℋ: π_1((X,d_X,𝒢),x) -> π_1((Y,d_Y,ℋ),y).
'Soit alors γ̇ l'image de γ dans ℋ' (script H) rather than plain H.
'Nous allons expliciter cet isomorphisme' is correctly read; 'lacets' is struck out and replaced by 'chemins'.
'lacet dans x autour de a' is likely meant as a loop based at x around a.
